newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices end mostly down on caution.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices end mostly down on caution.

text.p: China's A and B share indices ended mostly down on Friday on jitters over the possible announcement at the weekend of measures aimed at cooling the markets, brokers said.
But the Shanghai B share index ended up marginally on institutional buying in blue-chips, they said, adding that other stocks largely languished pending the release of the bulk of the 1996 results.
Of 43 B share companies, less than 10 have so far issued annual results with the April 30 deadline approaching.
The B index edged up 0.218 points or 0.3 percent to 73.320 on volume of 13.2 million shares worth $8.1 million.
Some overseas funds were seen flowing into the market as a result of the recent strong performance by Chinese stocks listed in Hong Kong, brokers said.
"The market will rise further if more overseas capital flows into the market," another broker said.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Cashmere Products was the star on institutional buying, jumping $0.044 or 5.83 percent to $0.798 on volume of 1.3 million shares.
Another blue-chip, portable phone maker Eastern Communications, traded the most on overseas buying, up $0.032 or 3.14 percent at $1.050 on volume of 1.5 million shares.
The Shenzhen B share index slipped 1.34 points or 0.84 percent to close at 157.34 on turnover of HK$72.83 million, eroded by losses in A shares, brokers said.
The A index slid 7.90 points or 1.71 percent to 453.62 on turnover of 9.55 billion yuan against 10.67 billion in the previous session.
"B shares were dragged down by the A shares which were hurt by talk that Beijing was drafting anti-speculation measures," a trader with Shenzhen J&A Securities (HK) Ltd said.
"Disappointing dividend plans by some B share firms also contributed to the day's retreat," an analyst at Sun Hung Kai Investment Services in Shenzhen said.
Conglomerate Shenzhen Zhonghao was the worst performer on the B share market, diving HK$0.30 or 6.82 percent to HK$4.10 on volume of 28,300 shares.
Guangdong Electric Power traded the most on 1.57 million shares and closed up HK$0.08 at HK$7.68 after the firm announced solid 1996 results.

The Shanghai A share index dipped 3.709 points or 0.28 percent to 1,340.593 on volume of 875.6 million shares worth 11.0 billion yuan. The SSE30 index fell 23.500 points or 0.66 percent to 3,512.598 points.
Chongqing Department Store was the biggest loser on institutional selling, down 1.37 yuan or 6.77 percent to 18.85 yuan on volume of 2.9 million shares.
